chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Jammilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Muhammad al-Halabi and Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them), who said:

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And remember your Lord if you forget.' He said: 'When a man takes an oath and forgets to include the condition (of God willing), he should include it when he remembers.'

key_terms.الاسْتِثْنَاء: The condition 'Insha'Allah' (if God wills) added to an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to say 'Insha'Allah' while taking an oath?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the practical application of Surah Al-A'raf 7:54, linking the general command to 'remember' specifically to the omission of *Insha'Allah* in oaths. It establishes the juristic principle that forgetting to include the condition of divine will does not invalidate the oath nor require expiation (*kaffarah*), provided the person recalls and states it immediately upon remembrance. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease in religious obligations and the distinction between intentional violation and simple forgetfulness.
